conviction_note: Ten-month trading update (Jan-Oct 2026) at 07:00 on 18 Nov; the bar is the company's own compiled FY26 adj. PBT consensus of GBP49.7m (range 48.0-50.5), which needs H2 adj. PBT of ~GBP24.8m vs GBP21.7m in H2 2025 (+14%) while both listed brick peers have cut since (Ibstock 2 Nov, Forterra 11 Nov) and October housebuilding PMI fell to 35.1. Marshalls' own self-help (Landscaping savings, H1 segment profit +GBP5.2m) gives a plausible path to 'unchanged', so the distribution is skewed (likely small relief or small fall on an in-line print, with a ~1-in-3 tail of a lower-end/below steer worth -8 to -12%). That gives p_up 45 on abs 5.5, so the scaled number is -0.55 against a findings sum of -1.4. The gap is the skew: the findings sum is the expected value of the tail, and p_up counts how often the stock closes up.

new_in_release.expect: Ten-month revenue, with Jul-Oct revenue by segment, not seen by the market. I expect group revenue down roughly 2-3% YTD and Jul-Oct down mid-single digits, with Building Products (54% new housing) and Marley weakest and Landscaping roughly flat on share gains. Direction negative, magnitude uncertain.

The FY26 adj. PBT steer against the GBP49.7m consensus. Base case is 'unchanged / in line' (~60%), resting on Landscaping self-help. A 'lower end of range' or 'below' steer is ~35%; I see no plausible route to an upgrade (~5%).
Pre-IFRS16 net debt at Oct (GBP155m a year earlier); the company has said it expects to de-lever in 2026. Expect lower year on year; mildly positive.
Commentary on Your First Home (start delayed to Apr 2027) and on 2027 pricing. Unknown.

findings.finding: Both listed UK brick and clay peers cut guidance inside Marshalls' reporting period. Ibstock (2 Nov): UK brick market volumes down ~17% year on year in Jul-Aug, Q3 brick sales 22% below expectations, weakness continuing into October, H2 'materially below'. Forterra (11 Nov): brick despatches down 11% over nine months, ten-month LFL revenue down 11.9% against down 9.3% in H1, RMI demand 'broadly in line with that for new-build', FY EBITDA c.GBP50m against GBP54.8m consensus. Both blame the Your First Home scheme being delayed to April 2027 for near-term demand. Marshalls' Building Products takes 54% of revenue from new housing and Landscaping 28%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marshalls' own guidance cut on 2025-07-25 moved it -20.64%. Its in-line reiterations moved +0.35% (Nov 2025 ten-month update) and +2.94% (May 2026 AGM). MSLH rose 3.0% on Ibstock's warning day and fell 2.6% on Forterra's.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MSLH is -4.6% over 5 sessions and fell 2.6% on the Forterra day. But it ROSE 3% on the Ibstock warning day and still trades about where it did after the H1 print (~172p against 177p). Had the market priced a Marshalls cut, the 3-7-analyst consensus would show downgrades after 2 Nov, and none is visible (the company's broker page is still dated 10 Aug). Forterra also undercuts the 'Marshalls is RMI-shielded' argument by saying RMI is as weak as new-build.
findings.independence: Forterra ten-month update, a different issuer and a different document: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/forterra--fort/trading-update/9868628 (2026-11-11). Both are peers, not counterparties.

findings.finding: Marshalls' main route to market contracted sharply in its H2. Travis Perkins Q3 merchanting like-for-like VOLUME was -9.0% (price/mix +6.8%), 'most notably in new build residential'. The October construction PMI fell to 43.6, with housebuilding at 35.1 (from 40.7) on rising borrowing costs. Marshalls' Jul-Oct revenue is therefore likely to be negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At H1 2026 a 0.5% revenue slip outweighed a 13% PBT beat and the stock fell 6.78%. At the Nov 2025 ten-month update revenue of +2% with expectations unchanged moved it +0.35%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are a merchant's and a survey's numbers, not Marshalls'. Marshalls' Jul-Oct revenue has never been printed, and the H1 reaction shows the market prices this name on revenue as well as profit. If it were priced, the stock would sit below its post-H1 level, and it does not.
findings.independence: S&P Global/CIPS October construction PMI, a public survey: https://www.itv.com/news/2026-11-05/construction-activity-falls-on-slump-in-housebuilding-amid-severe-headwinds (2026-11-05). Genuit (20 Oct) is mixed: water LFL down 3.3% but new-house completions 'resilient'. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/genuit-group--gen/trading-update/9830631

findings.finding: Marshalls' FY26 bar rests mostly on self-help that does not need volume. Landscaping segment profit rose from GBP0.3m to GBP5.5m in H1 on the GBP11m annualised savings plan (about GBP3m realised in 2025, the rest by end FY26). Landscaping made only ~GBP0.3m in H2 2025, so the ~GBP3.1m H2 PBT step-up that consensus needs is within reach of savings and lower finance costs even if Building Products and Marley soften.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In-line reiterations moved +0.35% (Nov 2025) and +2.94% (May 2026), but -6.78% at H1 2026 when revenue slipped.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the company's own guided path, so it is largely inside the guidance already given and sized near zero. Its only unpriced part is that, after two peer warnings, an in-line steer would be a relative relief. Ibstock itself rebounded 6.2% on 17 Nov, which shows the sector is short-covered and sensitive to that.
findings.independence: FY25 results put the network savings at GBP11m annualised, about GBP3m of it in 2025: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/marshalls--mslh/final-results/9474629 (2026-03-16). It comes from the same issuer, so it is not independent of the guide.

findings.finding: UK domestic RMI retail held up in Marshalls' H2: Wickes Q3 retail revenue +6.0% (LFL +5.6%) 'with notable strength in timber, flooring, roofing and garden', and Howdens' UK sales were +6.8% reported in periods 7-11 to 31 Oct. Marshalls' Landscaping takes 28-29% of revenue from housing RMI and Marley is weighted to RMI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no Marshalls-specific history on an RMI read-across
findings.why_not_priced: It is a retail DIY proxy and Marshalls sells mainly through merchants and contractors. Forterra (11 Nov) says RMI extension demand is as weak as new-build, which partly contradicts it, so the finding is kept small.
